posts.name: Chaosmancer
posts.cooked:
Yak Guardian:

Ignoring Iron Legacy (who is more of a mega-villain) and Vengeful 5 (who aren't intended to be played in the standard fashion) there are six** heroes without a major (i.e. Villain Card + 25-card deck) Nemesis Villain. Assuming Wrath is 2H/4V/2E as the previous expansions, and assuming that the 2 Heroes have their Nemesis in the set, and assuming that the other 2 Villains match up with previous Heroes, (OK that's a lot of [CENSORED] assuming) we'd still need 4 more Villains to complete the Nemesis match-ups, which seems like something that they would be likely to do. So 1 standard expansion (Wrath) and 1 mega (with 4 Nemesis Villains and enough unknown stuff to count as a "Mega") does seem to make sense. Mind you, I'd love to see a new expansions come out on a regular basis for as long as >G can come up with cool stuff for us (which seems likely to be forever), but the 1 standard + 1 mega fits what we already have and already know. **(Absolute Zero, Bunker, K.N.Y.F.E., The Naturalist, The Scholar, and Unity for those who don't have a quick reference sheet in front of them) 

 

From the Naturalist's artwork, incap and when he is a rhino getting blasted, the reptile headed guy in WotC will most likely be his nemesis. That leaves either Captain Cosmic or Skyscraper (I am assuming but I feel confident) wthout a nemesis in WotC

My guess is that the Cosmic Entity is going to be a) Captain Cosmic's nemesis, and b) in Wrath of the Cosmos.

 

Regarding Foote's predictions:  I doubt the last set will have no heroes, which would imply that current villians would get hero decks.  I suspect that the Matriarch and the Operative would be two, but I don't know about the other 2 or 3.

 

Alternatively, they could add a Vengance Mini expansion (minimini expansion?), and then have the freedom to create 5 new heroes (they could still be converted villians, but they'd have their own nemesis symbols).  Which would mean that the mega expansion would have 9 or 10 villians.  Which is a bit much, but I wouldn't complain.

As far as the highest stakes go, I gotta believe the cosmic entity (or however it is implimented in the narrative) is the only thing (that we currently know of) with "final showdown" weight behind it.
